researchCoverage.question: Which official web-platform and accessibility authorities govern the application document, controls, events, storage, files, and phone rendering? Which external authority governs SHA-256 over exact bytes? Which first-party GitHub documentation governs Pages publication and Actions execution? What independent evidence establishes non-circular requirements, reliable structured records, project persistence, execution isolation, verification coverage, and exact release identity?

researchCoverage.performanceEvidence: Recorded through the current application project model and corroborated by repository, browser, and workflow evidence.

findings.statement: A standalone browser application can use native HTML controls, DOM events, local storage, files, and downloads while remaining a single HTML artifact.
findings.exactEvidence: Applicable normative and first-party sections were preserved in the Stage 2 source records.
findings.applicability: The product is a phone-first standalone browser application.
findings.obligations: Use valid document structure, operable native controls, and observable state transitions.
findings.prohibitions: Do not depend on hidden external UI assets for the released standalone HTML.
findings.conditions: Browser support and storage availability must be verified.
findings.quantitativeLimits: Phone viewport widths of 320 and 393 CSS pixels are explicitly exercised.
findings.requiredProcedures: Render and interact through the actual browser UI.
findings.safetyQuality: Preserve accessible labels and visible state.
findings.currentFacts: Current Chromium execution is used for rendered verification.
findings.verificationImplications: Static checks and phone-width browser execution are both required.
findings.performanceEvidence: Recorded through the current application project model and corroborated by repository, browser, and workflow evidence.

findings.statement: SHA-256 must be computed over the exact product bytes that are audited and released.
findings.exactEvidence: Cryptographic digest authority and exact-byte procedures are represented by the registered external source.
findings.applicability: The release gate publishes a standalone HTML file.
findings.obligations: Compute and compare exact audited and release hashes.
findings.prohibitions: Do not release different bytes under an accepted decision.
findings.conditions: Exact byte source and length must be preserved.
findings.dependencies: Web Crypto or equivalent deterministic SHA-256 implementation.
findings.requiredProcedures: Hash the exact attached product bytes.
findings.safetyQuality: Hash equality is necessary but not sufficient; all prior audits must pass.
findings.currentFacts: The current application exposes exact product byte hashing.
findings.verificationImplications: Stage 30 must prove product, audited, and release hashes are identical.
findings.performanceEvidence: Recorded through the current application project model and corroborated by repository, browser, and workflow evidence.

findings.statement: Pages deployment and Actions execution must follow first-party repository, permissions, artifact, and publication behavior and must verify the live bytes after deployment.
findings.exactEvidence: First-party GitHub documentation is registered in the source inventory.
findings.applicability: The required destination is a GitHub Pages project URL.
findings.obligations: Build, verify, upload, deploy, and compare live bytes to verified source bytes.
findings.prohibitions: Do not treat a successful workflow start as proof of live byte identity.
findings.conditions: Pages and Actions must be enabled for the repository.
findings.dependencies: Repository permissions and GitHub-hosted workflow execution.

productionInstructions.objective: Build and deploy the complete phone-first, domain-general Closed-Loop Agent Reliability application defined by the corrected build instruction, with the exact 31-stage workflow, strict non-circular external research, complete structured project records, first-class human and agent work ownership, independent verification and correction, exact release hashing, and a retained completed project about the application itself that remains visible in Projects.
productionInstructions.governingInputs: INPUT-001 through INPUT-003; registered external sources; REQ-001 through REQ-008; TEST-001 through TEST-008; MUTATION-001 through MUTATION-008.
productionInstructions.scope: The complete application, retained project, exact release files, and configured Pages deployment.
productionInstructions.orderedProcedure: Follow Stages 1 through 31 in order using structured records, current-schema project state, independent contexts, responsible-layer correction, product-byte verification, audits, decision, and release.
productionInstructions.decisionRules: Mandatory violations block acceptance. Confirmed defects invalidate dependent work. ACCEPTED requires complete affirmative evidence and passing validators.
productionInstructions.toolRules: Use actual external research systems, the real rendered browser UI, isolated browser contexts, deterministic scripts, SHA-256, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, and post-deploy live retrieval.
productionInstructions.outputContract: Standalone index.html; current-schema SELF_VERIFIED_PROJECT.json; verification reports; exact hashes; Pages deployment receipt.
productionInstructions.failureBehavior: Record BLOCKED or REJECTED rather than inventing evidence. Correct the earliest responsible layer and rerun dependent stages.
productionInstructions.truthSemantics: User inputs establish intent; external sources establish externally governed requirements; workflow records establish only what happened in the workflow.
productionInstructions.completionCriteria: The retained project appears in Projects after a clean load, is current-schema, is about the complete application, and has 31 COMPLETE stages. New projects begin at 0/31. The app exposes human, agent, and team ownership and structured work records, not a generic instruction-paste workflow. External-source guards reject internal artifacts as authority. All required ten-run sets and verification matrices exist. Confirmed defects are corrected and regressions pass. Product bytes are audited, hashes match, decision is ACCEPTED, exact artifacts are released, and the configured live URL serves the verified HTML and project JSON.
